assertion.rationale: F9 (Task 13, partial close): resource-plane actions are now traceable. The subscription Activity Log (layer-06-platform.yml) captures the caller identity behind every ARM create/update/delete in the estate (Administrative category); Key Vault diagnosticSettings captures AuditEvent (who read/wrote which secret, key, certificate); SQL auditSettings with isAzureMonitorTargetEnabled:true captures per-principal database activity; storage and CAE diagnosticSettings cover the rest of the Azure resource plane — all landing in the same Log Analytics workspace platform/main.bicep wires. What is NOT traceable: the directory/identity plane itself. Entra SignInLogs and AuditLogs remain unrouted (Task 13 recorded this as needing live-tenant verification of the Microsoft.aadiam resource shape and the Entra role required, rather than shipping unverified syntax), so which human or workload identity actually authenticated, which Conditional Access policy evaluated, and which directory role assignment changed are still not traceable anywhere in the estate. Traceability for what a principal DID once inside Azure is now real; traceability for WHO that principal was at the directory layer is not.

recommendation: Route Entra ID SignInLogs and AuditLogs to the Log Analytics workspace once the Microsoft.aadiam tenant-scoped resource shape and required Entra role can be verified against a live tenant — the one remaining contributor. The resource-plane half of this control (diagnosticSettings on Key Vault/storage/SQL/CAE, Activity Log) is DONE.
